title: Uniform Span Handoff Orchestrator: tenant-aware routing, compact envelopes & graceful backend fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a unified span handoff orchestrator that accepts OTLP spans and reliably routes them to downstream tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, external vendor endpoints) with tenant-aware priority lanes, compact envelope encoding to reduce bandwidth and storage, and deterministic graceful fallback to archival storage or low-cost collectors when backends are degraded.
background: We continue to see load spikes that cause backend Tempo clusters to throttle or OOM. Current per-client exporters either drop spans or block request paths. We need an intermediate, high-throughput component to smooth ingest, preserve high-priority spans, and provide multiple levels of degradation (compact, drop-low-priority, archive) while keeping trace reconstruction feasible for debugging and SLO analysis.
design_decisions: Use a fronting gRPC/HTTP OTLP endpoint that normalizes incoming batches and annotates spans with tenant priority metadata (derived from token+route).
Implement three delivery lanes: REALTIME (low latency, small batch windows), BULK (cost-optimized batching for lower priority), and ARCHIVE (append-only S3/GCS fallback).

Compact envelopes: run a deterministic delta-compression over repeated attributes and string interning per-batch; keep span ids and timestamps intact to allow rehydration for most debugging workflows.
Backpressure policy: if REALTIME lane is congested, dynamically promote critical spans (error:true OR latency>p99) into a promoted subset; non-critical spans move to BULK or ARCHIVE.
Ordering guarantees: best-effort ordering preserved per-trace by tagging sequence metadata; downstream reassembly handles out-of-order segments.
Idempotency and dedup: use a canonical span fingerprint + tenant + batch-hash to de-duplicate across retries without storing full payloads.
Security: TLS mutual auth for connections to third-party collectors; token exchange rotation mechanism for long-lived ingest agents.
Operational hooks: expose metrics for lane occupancy, stall_count, archive_rate, and per-tenant SLA breach counters.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Compaction vs fidelity: compact envelopes reduce cost but may strip transient span attributes needed for rare post-mortems. We mitigate by keeping an uncompressed sample window for each tenant.
Complexity: Introducing an orchestrator increases operational surface area and requires strong testing and playbooks for rollback.
Latency: REALTIME lane must preserve our <250ms span-handshake SLO; batching and compression must be tuned not to violate this for promoted spans.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Prototype fronting service accepts OTLP/gRPC and normalizes TraceData; demoed basic lane routing with in-memory queues. - Aisha
2026-02-20: Implemented compact envelope prototype using string interning and attribute delta encoding; achieved ~3x reduction in median payload size for our synthetic workload. - Marco

2026-02-26: Load test v0.2 against tempo-dev shows handoff throughput 2.5k spans/sec per vCPU with 8ms median enqueue latency. Identified GC hotspots in Go collector; switching to a pool-based encoder. - Marco

2026-03-03: Design review with PM & SRE. Agreed to add a sampled uncompressed buffer per tenant (10k spans) for forensic retrieval. Need a runbook for fail-open vs fail-closed during control-plane outage. - Notes from Dana (SRE)

2026-03-09: Integrated initial metrics exposure (prometheus) for lane_queue_length, archive_enqueue_rate, and backpressure_events. Added alert for sustained REALTIME queue length > 80% for >2m. - Marco
2026-03-12: Security review request uploaded. Confirmed mTLS path for external vendor endpoints and rotateable client cert mechanism required. - Aisha

Build e2e rehydration path to ensure compacted envelopes can restore trace segments for 99% of sampled cases
Implement SLO-driven retry budget and expose per-tenant throttling reasons to Console
Author rollback playbook and chaos test (partition downstream for 30m)
Add admin endpoints to manually adjust lane thresholds per-tenant
Finalize client cert rotation controller and document KMS integration
acceptance_criteria: Can route to Tempo and Jaeger endpoints with mTLS; test harness validates end-to-end trace reassembly for 95% of traces under typical load
REALTIME lane 95th percentile enqueue latency < 200ms at steady-state load; promoted critical spans observe <250ms end-to-end handoff
Compaction reduces median payload size by >=2x without breaking rehydration for sampled traces
System gracefully degrades: when downstream returns 429/503, >=90% of critical spans are retained and forwarded to ARCHIVE or BULK with documented TTL
Metrics & alerts created and wired to Console dashboards; per-tenant breach events visible in rollout console
